source: SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2 section 6.3 (Class B, longitudinal)

input_notes.manual_activation_s: Digitised from the SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2 v2.1 PDF at 250 dpi: the plot frame fixes both axes, the red 'Start BBA/FFFS' line fixes activation, and the HRR trace is the per-column median of the blue curve. Figures 27, 28 and 29 place the activation line at 167, 180 and 175 s. The previous 300 s had no source and ran the unsuppressed pool fire two minutes longer than the test did.
input_notes.velocity_ms: Digitised from the SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2 v2.1 PDF at 250 dpi: the plot frame fixes both axes, the red 'Start BBA/FFFS' line fixes activation, and the velocity is the per-column median of the five coloured height traces. Annex 2 gives no velocity in words for this test. The value follows the convention the c4 and c5 anchors already use, which take section 6.1's '2-2,5 m/s' and section 6.2's '1-1,5 m/s' -- the U45 velocity while the fire burns, not the fans' pre-fire duty: Figure 10 reads 2.31 m/s over c4's 420-900 s, matching its anchor's 2.25. Figure 28 reads 2.44 m/s over 175-300 s and 2.30 m/s over 300-480 s, so 2.35 m/s; before the fire it read 3.7 m/s. The previous 1.5 m/s had no source.

measured_notes.backlayering: Read off the U15 thermocouple tree, as Annex 2 judged it: Figure 29, 'A strong backlayering before the activation of the FFFS can be observed', peaking near 190 C at 5.0 m just before activation; section 6.3: 'The fire created a large back layering of smoke which completely disappeared shortly after activation'.
measured_notes.pools_extinguished: Section 6.3: 'After a few minutes the fire was extinguished pool by pool', and the pools were re-ignited afterwards, which 'ensures that the fire was extinguished by the FFFS and not by a lack of fuel'. Figure 27 has the HRR down to about 2 MW by roughly 570 s.
